summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to generate embeddings for dermatology images. These embeddings facilitate the development of AI models for skin image analysis, requiring less data and computation than traditional methods [SOURCE 1].
intended_use_and_workflow: Derm Foundation reduces the resources needed to develop models for skin image analysis. Embeddings can be used for tasks like classifying skin conditions (psoriasis, melanoma, dermatitis), scoring severity, identifying body parts, and assessing image quality [SOURCE 4].
model_limitations: The model's quality can degrade in extreme lighting or noise conditions. The fine-tuned model was trained on data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia) and settings (mostly clinical), which may affect its generalizability [SOURCE 4].
model_type: The model is a BiT-M ResNet101x3 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) [SOURCE 4].
training_data: The model was trained in two stages: initially using contrastive learning on image-text pairs from the internet and then fine-tuned for condition classification using clinical datasets from the US, Colombia, Australia, and additional public images [SOURCE 4].
validation_test_dataset: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across various skin-related classification tasks. Training a linear classifier on Derm Foundation embeddings showed a 10-15% increase in accuracy compared to a standard BiT-M model [SOURCE 4].
